testName: Air Brakes Test #1 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Air entering air storage tanks may contain:
questions.explanation: Air entering storage tanks contains water and compressor oil. These materials can damage the braking system. Tanks have drains to remove them.

questions.question: In cold weather, check and fill the alcohol evaporator:
questions.explanation: An alcohol evaporator prevents ice buildup in air brake systems. Check and refill it every day in cold weather.

questions.question: While driving, ____ holds spring brakes in place.
questions.explanation: Air pressure holds spring brakes in place while driving. If air pressure drops low enough, the springs will activate the brakes.

questions.question: During an applied leakage test, what is the maximum safe leakage rate for a single vehicle with air brakes?
questions.explanation: A single vehicle with air brakes should have a leakage rate no higher than 3 psi in one minute during an applied leakage test.

questions.question: During an applied leakage test, the maximum leakage rate for a single vehicle with air brakes is:
questions.explanation: A single vehicle with air brakes should have a leakage rate no higher than 3 psi in one minute during an applied leakage test.

questions.question: Air tank drains:

options.text: Should not be used in cold weather.
Remove water and oil from the air tanks.
Clean the air in the passenger compartment.

questions.correctAnswerText: Remove water and oil from the air tanks.
questions.explanation: Air tank drains remove water and compressor oil from the system. Letting these materials build up can damage the brakes. Use manual drains daily.

questions.question: A low air pressure warning signal:

options.text: Is not recommended on vehicles with air brakes.
Is required on vehicles with air brakes.
Is optional on vehicles with air brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is required on vehicles with air brakes.
questions.explanation: All vehicles with air brakes must have a low air pressure warning signal.

questions.question: When the brake pedal is pressed, air brakes work:

options.text: Only if the green lever on the control panel is pushed down.

questions.explanation: Air brakes take a half-second or more to work after the brake pedal is pressed. Air must travel through the lines to activate the brakes. This is different from hydraulic brakes, which work instantly.

questions.question: If the ABS warning light comes on while driving, it means:

options.text: The ABS has just been activated.
The ABS is not working properly.
The ABS needs to be activated.

questions.correctAnswerText: The ABS is not working properly.
questions.explanation: Vehicles with Anti-Lock Braking Systems have yellow warning lights. When these lights come on, there is a problem with the braking system. You may have lost ABS on one or more wheels.

questions.question: Truck tractors with air brakes built on or after March 1, 1997 must have:
questions.explanation: Truck tractors with air brakes built on or after March 1, 1997 must have anti-lock brakes. Other vehicles with air brakes built on or after March 1, 1998 must also have them.

questions.question: What do air tank drains do?

options.text: Let rain water into the tanks.
Remove water and oil from the air tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Remove water and oil from the air tanks.
questions.explanation: Compressed air contains water and compressor oil. These can damage the brakes if they build up. You must open air tank drains every day to remove this buildup.

questions.question: What does a one-way check valve do?

options.text: Drains water and compressor oil from the air tanks.
Stops air from leaking out if the compressor breaks.
Turns on the emergency brakes when there is a leak.
Keeps the spring brakes in place until used.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stops air from leaking out if the compressor breaks.
questions.explanation: A one-way check valve sits between the air compressor and the first main tank. It prevents air from escaping if the compressor leaks.

questions.question: Where are ABS warning lights on trucks and buses?

options.text: On the outside of the vehicle near the passenger door

questions.explanation: Trucks and buses with Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS) have yellow warning lights on the instrument panel. Trailers have yellow ABS lights on the left side, at the front or rear corner.

questions.question: What must truck tractors with air brakes built after March 1, 1997 have?
questions.explanation: All truck tractors with air brakes built on or after March 1, 1997 must have Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS).

questions.question: Why were front brake limiting valves designed?

options.text: To keep the front tires from skidding.
To keep the front tires from getting too hot.
To use the brakes equally on all wheels.

questions.correctAnswerText: To keep the front tires from skidding.
questions.explanation: Some older vehicles have front brake limiting valves. They were made to prevent front wheels from skidding. However, research showed these devices are not needed, so they should be left in the normal position.

questions.question: When does front wheel braking work?
questions.explanation: Front wheel braking works well in all road conditions. You are unlikely to experience front wheel skid, even on ice.

questions.question: How should you stop in an emergency?

options.text: Lock the wheels and skid to a stop.
Brake while keeping your vehicle in a straight line.
Expect the vehicle to slow down faster than normal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake while keeping your vehicle in a straight line.
questions.explanation: In an emergency stop, use controlled braking or stab braking. Keep your vehicle in a straight line while braking. You should still be able to steer if needed.

questions.question: What do both systems in a dual air brake system share?
questions.explanation: Both systems in a dual air brake system use the same air compressor. If the compressor fails, neither system will work.

questions.question: What does an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) do?

options.text: Is not available for vehicles with air brakes.
Is not helpful in most driving situations.
Helps you keep control when braking.

questions.correctAnswerText: Helps you keep control when braking.
questions.explanation: Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS) work with air brakes and help drivers stay in control by preventing the wheels from locking up.

questions.question: What is the maximum air leakage for a single vehicle during a static leakage test in one minute?
questions.explanation: For a single vehicle with air brakes, the leakage rate should not exceed 2 psi in one minute. If it does, something needs to be fixed and the vehicle should not be driven.

questions.question: When can a driver rely on front wheel braking to work?
questions.explanation: Front wheel braking works well in all road conditions. Front wheels rarely skid, even on ice.

questions.question: What type of brakes do most new heavy-duty trucks have?
questions.explanation: Most new heavy-duty trucks use dual air brake systems. This system has two separate air brake systems that share one set of brake controls.

questions.question: How many air storage tanks does an air brake system use?
questions.explanation: Air storage tanks hold compressed air. Different vehicles have different numbers and sizes of air tanks in their brake systems.

questions.question: What do air tank drains do?

options.text: Let rainwater into the air tanks.
Remove water and oil from the air tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Remove water and oil from the air tanks.
questions.explanation: Air tank drains allow water and compressor oil to be removed from the system. Water and oil buildup can damage the air brake system.

questions.question: What does the application pressure gauge show?

options.text: How much air pressure is being sent to the brakes.
The temperature of the air in the brake system.
The pressure of air from the compressor.
How many times the brakes have been used.

questions.correctAnswerText: How much air pressure is being sent to the brakes.
questions.explanation: The application pressure gauge shows how much air pressure is being sent to the brakes. Not all vehicles with air brakes have this gauge.
